questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U05_L02_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.SYS.3

What boundary style is used for y < 2x + 1?

feedback.text: Correct. Strict inequalities use dashed boundaries because equality is not included.
Solid boundaries include equality.
A graph needs the related boundary line.
An inequality has a region, not one point.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U05_L02_GP_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.SYS.3

What boundary style is used for y >= -x + 3?

feedback.text: Dashed means equality is not included.
Correct. The symbol >= includes equality, so the boundary is included.
The related equation is still graphed.
The full boundary line is needed.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U05_L02_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.SYS.3

Which point satisfies y <= x + 2?

feedback.text: 5 <= 3 is false.
4 <= 2 is false.
Correct. Substitute to get 3 <= 3, which is true.
4 <= 1 is false.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U05_L02_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.SYS.3

For y > x - 1, which side is shaded?

feedback.text: Below would match less than.
Strict inequality excludes the boundary line.
Every inequality shades a half-plane.
Correct. Greater than means y-values above the boundary.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: ALG2_U05_L02_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.A2.SYS.3

What is a feasible region?

answer.text: The overlap of all solution regions

feedback.text: Correct. A system solution must satisfy every inequality.
All constraints must be used.
The feasible region is usually an area.

answer.text: Any point on the coordinate plane

feedback.text: Not every point satisfies the constraints.
